description: Biopterin family covering 6 redox/protonation states from fully oxidized BIO through the tetrahydro/cation-radical/N5-radical/quinonoid-dihydro/7,8-dihydro forms. Used for nitric-oxide synthase, phenylalanine hydroxylase, and other pterin-dependent enzymes.
methodology: Fragment-typed force-field parameters for the biopterin family across six redox and protonation states (fully oxidized biopterin, tetrahydro, cation radical, N5 radical, quinonoid-dihydro, and 7,8-dihydro), AMBER ff14SB/ff19SB-compatible. The chemistry parameterized de novo is the pterin saturated face (N5, N8, C6, C7) together with the dihydroxypropyl side chain, given fragment-scoped atom types per state; the aromatic pyrimidinone face inherits ff14SB nucleic-acid types. Partial charges are whole-molecule, two-stage restrained (Bayly) RESP fits to a gas-phase HF/6-31G(d) Merz-Kollman ESP at four RBRA reorientations on a B3LYP/6-31+G(d) PCM(water) geometry, with unrestricted references for the open-shell cation-radical and N5-radical states. Bonds and angles for the saturated face and side chain are Seminario fits to the B3LYP/6-31+G(d)/PCM(water) QM Hessian, taking interior terms from capped-fragment Hessians and cross-fragment junction terms from the whole-residue Hessian. Proper dihedrals are full multi-term GAFF2 potentials transferred by atom-type substitution and improper planarity terms are the standard AMBER terms perceived by tLEaP with pyramidal sp3 centers omitted; neither dihedral class is QM-derived. Biopterin carries no phosphate or nucleotide, so no Meagher or Walker parameters are involved. Every frcmod is a delta-only file layered on parm10/gaff2.
references: Fragment-typed cofactor force-field library, v1.0 (20 redox-active residues across the FMN, FAD, NADP, NAD, and biopterin families). See the 'methodology' field for the full derivation. Non-redox-active atoms use established AMBER parameters (ff14SB nucleic acids, Walker NAD+ contrib, Meagher polyphosphate).
Walker NAD+ contrib parameters (Walker, in AmberTools dat/contrib/NADH_and_NAD+/).
ff14SB nucleic acid types from parm10 + bsc1 + OL3 dihedrals (leaprc.RNA.OL3).

Guberman_H4B_RESP.description: Constrained-geometry-optimization RESP charges + Seminario bonded parameters on redox-active fragment atoms + validated AMBER libraries (ff14SB / Walker NAD+ / Meagher polyphosphate) for non-redox-active atoms. Multi-cofactor-safe by construction (cross-residue same-fragment-type bonds are bit-identical).
Guberman_H4B_RESP.reference: Fragment-typed cofactor force field library, v1.0. 20 redox-active residues across FMN, FAD, NADP, NAD, and biopterin families. Each residue's frcmod is self-contained (merged from per-fragment Seminario frcmod + cofactor-to-protein linker + residue-specific cross-source params + cross-residue patches). with validated AMBER libs (ff14SB nucleic acids, Walker NAD+ contrib, Meagher polyphosphate) for non-redox-active atoms.
Guberman_H4B_RESP.name: Tetrahydrobiopterin (H4B)
Guberman_H4B_RESP.methodology:
This is a 'lean' add-on parameter file (an AMBER frcmod): it holds ONLY the force-field terms that the standard base force fields (loaded first) do not already supply, so nothing is duplicated. Here the base is ff14SB/parm10 (standard protein and nucleic types); no extra force fields are needed (biopterin has no phosphate). A force field models the molecule's energy with a few simple terms; here is where each one came from, in plain terms:

- Atomic charges (the partial electric charge on each atom, which sets the electrostatic forces) come from RESP, the standard recipe that adjusts the charges until they reproduce the molecule's quantum-mechanical (QM) electrostatic field. The field is sampled (Merz-Kollman scheme) over four molecular orientations and averaged, then fit in the usual two-stage (Bayly-Cieplak) way, held to the molecule's whole-number net charge. Charges were fit separately for each oxidation/protonation state and are unchanged by the atom-type relabeling below.
- Custom atom types: the redox-active ring atoms are given short custom type names so each state's distinct chemistry stays separate from the standard regions. This relabeling is value-neutral (a custom type keeps the same charge and atom 'size' as the type its atoms had before) and the types' element + hybridization are registered up front so implicit-solvent (Born) radii come out right.
- Van der Waals (each atom's effective size and 'stickiness', i.e. its Lennard-Jones radius and well depth): inherited unchanged from the source type each custom type maps to; no new values are invented.
- Bond and angle stiffness (how hard it is to stretch a bond or bend an angle, plus their rest values): from the Seminario method, which reads these constants directly off the QM second-derivative matrix (the 'Hessian') of the optimized geometry, instead of using rule-of-thumb estimates. Terms wholly inside the redox ring use an isolated-fragment Hessian; terms at a junction (where the ring meets a standard region, or where two base force fields meet) get a fresh value from the whole-molecule Hessian so the cross-boundary coupling is captured.
- Dihedrals/torsions (the energy of twisting around a bond): the Hessian gives only bonds/angles, so torsions are taken as complete (untruncated) Fourier series from the transferable GAFF2 torsion library by atom-type analogy, except the six-membered pterin rings, which are purine-like and so use the parm10 nucleic ring-fusion torsions.
- Impropers (small terms that keep flat groups flat): read from a clean build of the conventionally-typed molecule (one per planar center) and mapped onto the custom types; an improper is dropped where the QM geometry shows that center is actually pyramidal (e.g. a ring nitrogen in a reduced state), so a genuinely puckered atom is not wrongly flattened.

Geometry was a DFT optimization (one conformer per state). Every state was checked to build a complete tleap topology with no missing parameters.

References: Seminario 1996 (bonded constants from the QM Hessian); Bayly-Cieplak-Cornell-Kollman 1993 (two-stage RESP).

prerequisites.leaprc_groups_notes: Lean (delta-only) frcmod: needs only a standard AMBER protein FF (ff14SB->parm10 or ff19SB->parm19) for the parm10 base types and the parm10-nucleic ring-fusion dihedrals, plus addAtomTypes registration of the custom fragment types (emitted from atom_types). No gaff2, no meagher, no other leaprc.
